prediction.likelyOutcome: The tenants are likely to prevail on their breach of the repair and insurance covenant claims, recovering roughly the $19,365 they documented in repair and premium costs, while defeating Griffith's $25,000 roof-damage counterclaim and his unsupported oral triple-net lease/fraud theory. Net result favors the tenants, likely bolstered by prevailing-party attorney's fees given the unaccepted $20,000 Rule 68 offer, though the good-faith/fair-dealing and unjust enrichment theories add little incremental dollar value beyond the documented repair costs.

outcome.description: After a two-day bench trial the court held the written lease governed, found the landlord breached its insurance and maintenance covenants, and awarded the tenants $19,330 in damages (2016-2017 insurance premiums and the 2016 roof-failure repair and painting costs; earlier claims were time-barred), dismissed the landlord's claims, and awarded the tenants $59,604.75 in attorney's fees under Civil Rule 68, for a final judgment of $85,895.62. The Alaska Supreme Court affirmed on December 16, 2022.
